newsitem.title: UK: Talks fail to end Northern Ireland jail dispute.
newsitem.headline: Talks fail to end Northern Ireland jail dispute.

text.p: Protestant "Loyalist" prisoners came down from the rooftops at a troubled Northern Irish prison on Wednesday but talks failed to end a two-day dispute about new security procedures.
A politician who put the prisoners' complaints to government officials said no agreement had been reached and that more talks would be held on Thursday.

"Unfortunately we were not able to resolve the situation," John White, of the Loyalist Ulster Democratic Party, told reporters. "We put proposals on the table and we are having a meeting tomorrow to continue our discussions."

Earlier prison sources said staff who were withdrawn for their own protection on Tuesday had not yet been sent back into two wings of the Maze prison near Belfast where the trouble flared. They said they would not consider the dispute over until officers returned and reassumed control.
Before his talks with officials, White, whose UDP group has political links with the jailed pro-British guerrillas, said the prisoners had returned to their wings.
"The electricity supply has been restored and I am hoping that food and medication can be delivered to the prisoners," he told BBC radio.

"I am hoping that a line of communication can be installed whereby the prisoners can speak to the prison staff. At this moment, the prison staff are not prepared to go into the wings to talk to the prisoners."
Overnight, British officials had urged prison staff to step up personal security after outlawed Loyalist militants threatened violence if the authorities used force to end the dispute.

The protesters, called loyalist because of their fierce allegiance to continued British rule in Northern Ireland, tried to burn down two watchtowers on Tuesday and started another fire on Wednesday when they clambered on to the roof in the early hours.
The prisoners were objecting to tightened security measures brought in after the discovery last month of an escape tunnel that foiled a breakout plan by Irish Republican Army prisoners.
Loyalists say that they are being unfairly punished for the IRA's wrong-doing.
The Maze is Europe's biggest guerrilla prison complex, housing some 500 inmates, segregated according to loyalist or republican allegiance.
